Research Areas



Virome Ecology
Understanding how viruses shape ecological communities across natural and agricultural systems.



Plant Virology
Discovering, characterizing, and tracking plant viruses using genomics and molecular biology.



Bioinformatics
Developing reproducible computational methods for sequence analysis and pathogen discovery.






Disease Ecology
Studying pathogen dynamics across hosts, landscapes, and ecosystems.



Microbiome Ecology
Investigating interactions among viruses, fungi, bacteria, oomycetes, nematodes, and plants.



Forest Pathology
Understanding emerging diseases affecting forest ecosystems through ecology and genomics.

Dr. Ricardo I. Alcalá Briseño is an Assistant Professor of Viral Ecology in the Department of Plant Pathology and Environmental Microbiology at Penn State University. His research focuses on plant and fungal viruses, disease ecology, and the application of high-throughput sequencing and bioinformatics to understand pathogen emergence and transmission. He received his Ph.D. in Plant Pathology from the University of Florida and completed postdoctoral training at Oregon State University. His laboratory investigates virome dynamics and host impact in agricultural systems and forest ecosystems to improve disease detection, management, and ecosystem health.
His laboratory develops computational approaches for studying viromes, investigates virus–host interactions, and applies high-throughput sequencing to questions in disease ecology, microbial community assembly, and pathogen evolution.

The Briseño Lab investigates questions at the interface of ecology, evolution, and genomics, including:

Virus connectivity within host-associated systems
Microbiome and virome interactions
Ecology and evolution of plant viromes
Virus host impact and comparative genomics
Bioinformatics tool development
Pathogen surveillance using high-throughput sequencing






Viral Ecology (PPEM 454)





Representative software developed by the laboratory includes:

HoboR https://leboldus-lab.github.io/hoboR/
ViNA (Virome Network Analysis, coming soon)
Bioinformatics workflows for virome analysis
